editorial_reason: ProofWiki separately sources the discrete-time filtered measurable space construction: sub-σ-algebras are indexed by time, and inclusion is nondecreasing. The filtration does not itself require a probability measure; when paired with a probability space it forms a filtered probability space. This is not the complete, right-continuous or usual-conditions filtration. The direct continuous-time filtration locator was not accessible in this session and requires renewed source inspection before any additional continuous-time variant can be source-ingested.

ProofWiki separately displays discrete and continuous-time adapted-process definitions. Their structural shared meaning is measurability of X at each time with respect to information up to that time, but the different index sets remain separately labeled. An adapted process need not be a martingale, Markov process, or have sample-path continuity. Filtration and measurable-random-variable foundations remain independent prerequisites.

ProofWiki defines the σ-algebra-conditioned conditional expectation by integrability, G-measurability and matching integrals over each event A∈G; essential uniqueness is a separate theorem. The object is a random variable defined up to almost-sure equality, not a single number. Martingale equations are equality almost surely of such conditional expectation versions. This is not the simpler discrete expectation conditioned on a single positive-probability event.

The accessible ProofWiki Proper Vertex Coloring page explicitly defines the mapping to a palette of k colors and requires adjacent vertices receive unequal colors. The palette may have unused colors, and this is a vertex-coloring concept distinct from edge coloring. The chromatic number is the minimum k that admits such a coloring, so the source-screened proper coloring meaning will provide an exact noncircular prerequisite when separately reviewed.

The accessible ProofWiki formal definition allows an arbitrary index set and measurable state space. Sequences indexed by nonnegative integers and real-time indexed processes are special cases. The state-space measurability requirement is essential; merely taking an arbitrary family of functions without measurability would not satisfy the usual definition. Adaptedness is a separate property relative to a filtration.
